newsitem.title: USA: Tech spending seen growing fastest in LatAm.
newsitem.headline: Tech spending seen growing fastest in LatAm.

text.p: Spending in Latin America on computers and other information technology will grow at 18.2 percent a year through 2000, sharply above the 10.9 percent annual increases forecast for the sector worldwide, consultants International Data Corp said on Thursday.

Although accounting for only three percent of worldwide information technology expenditures, Latin America last year showed a 20.9 percent increase over 1995. The worldwide sector growth rate was 13.1 percent in 1996, International Data vice president Paul Pastrone told a technology marketing conference here.
"We're very, very optimistic that this train will stay on track and move very quickly," Pastrone said.

Pastrone said a survey of 722 large corporations throughout Latin America by International Data showed that only 10 percent of the big consumers of information technology planned to cut back during 1997, while 65 percent planned to increase spending on software, equipment and computer services. The remaining 25 percent said their spending would be unchanged from 1996.
